abda_4.name: Abda
abda_4.who: The father of Adoniram, the official who oversaw forced labor in Solomon's kingdom.
key: Abda is named as the father of Adoniram in the list of Solomon's high officials (1 Kings 4).
His son Adoniram was placed in charge of the forced labor for Solomon's building projects (1 Kings 4).

abdon_10.name: Abdon
abdon_10.who: A minor judge of Israel from Pirathon in Ephraim, son of Hillel, who judged Israel eight years.
key: After Elon, Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel (Judges 12).
He had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkeys (Judges 12).
After judging Israel eight years, he died and was buried at Pirathon in Ephraim (Judges 12).

abida_21.name: Abida
abida_21.who: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham through Keturah.
key: Abida is listed among the sons of Midian, Abraham's son by Keturah (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave his concubines' sons gifts and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).
Chronicles repeats Abida's name among Keturah's descendants (1 Chronicles 1).

abiezer_763.name: Abiezer
abiezer_763.who: A descendant of Manasseh through Gilead whose clan, the Abiezrites, produced the judge Gideon.
key: Iezer, ancestor of the clan of the Iezerites, is listed among the sons of Gilead (Numbers 26).
The clan of Abiezer received an allotment of land within the tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 17).
Gideon, son of Joash the Abiezrite, lived at Ophrah and rallied the Abiezrites to follow him (Judges 6).
Gideon calmed angry Ephraim by saying their gleanings outdid the vintage of Abiezer (Judges 8).

abigail_27.name: Abigail
abigail_27.who: A sister of David and Zeruiah, and the mother of Amasa, commander of Absalom's army.
key: She and Zeruiah are listed as sisters of David and his brothers (1 Chronicles 2).
She married Jether, also called Ithra, and bore him a son, Amasa (1 Chronicles 2).
Her son Amasa commanded Absalom's army during his revolt against David (2 Samuel 17).

abihail_31.name: Abihail
abihail_31.who: A daughter of Eliab, David's eldest brother, named in the family line of King Rehoboam's wife Mahalath.
key: Abihail was the daughter of Eliab son of Jesse, making her David's niece (2 Chronicles 11).
She is named in the parentage of Mahalath, who married Rehoboam and bore him three sons (2 Chronicles 11).

abijah_35.name: Abijah
abijah_35.who: A young son of King Jeroboam of Israel whose illness and death fulfilled the prophet Ahijah's word.
key: When Abijah fell sick, Jeroboam sent his wife in disguise to the prophet Ahijah at Shiloh (1 Kings 14).
Ahijah said the child would die, the only one of Jeroboam's house to be properly buried (1 Kings 14).
Ahijah said something pleasing to the LORD was found in him alone of Jeroboam's house (1 Kings 14).
The child died as his mother entered the house in Tirzah, and all Israel mourned him (1 Kings 14).

abijah_36.name: Abijah
abijah_36.who: A priest of David's time whose family formed the eighth priestly division, to which Zechariah later belonged.
key: When David organized the priests by lot, the eighth lot fell to Abijah (1 Chronicles 24).
Centuries later, Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, served as a priest of the division of Abijah (Luke 1).

abinadab_43.name: Abinadab
abinadab_43.who: A man of Kiriath-jearim who kept the ark of the covenant in his house for many years.
key: After the Philistines returned the ark, it was brought to Abinadab's house on the hill (1 Samuel 7).
His son Eleazar was consecrated to keep the ark, which stayed there twenty years (1 Samuel 7).
David moved the ark from Abinadab's house on a new cart driven by his sons Uzzah and Ahio (2 Samuel 6).
Chronicles also records the ark being carried out from Abinadab's house (1 Chronicles 13).

abinoam_46.name: Abinoam
abinoam_46.who: The father of Barak, the commander from Kedesh in Naphtali who fought Sisera alongside Deborah.
key: Deborah summoned his son Barak from Kedesh-naphtali to lead Israel against Sisera (Judges 4).
The Song of Deborah calls on Barak son of Abinoam to lead away his captives (Judges 5).

achsah_68.name: Achsah
achsah_68.who: The daughter of Caleb, given in marriage to Othniel after he captured Kiriath-sepher (Debir).
key: Caleb promised his daughter Achsah to the man who captured Kiriath-sepher (Joshua 15).
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, captured the city and married Achsah (Joshua 15).
She asked Caleb for springs of water, and he gave her the upper and lower springs (Joshua 15).
The account of her marriage and request for springs is repeated after Joshua's death (Judges 1).

adaiah_72.name: Adaiah
adaiah_72.who: A priest descended from Pashhur, son of Jeroham, who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile.
key: Adaiah son of Jeroham is listed among the priests who settled in Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chronicles 9).
Nehemiah's list of Jerusalem's residents also names him among the priests serving there (Nehemiah 11).

adoni-bezek_96.name: Adoni-bezek
adoni-bezek_96.who: A Canaanite king at Bezek defeated by Judah and Simeon after Joshua's death.
key: The men of Judah and Simeon defeated Adoni-bezek's forces at Bezek and captured him (Judges 1).
They cut off his thumbs and big toes, as he had done to seventy kings (Judges 1).
He acknowledged that God had repaid him, and he died after being brought to Jerusalem (Judges 1).

adoni-zedek_101.name: Adoni-zedek
adoni-zedek_101.who: The Amorite king of Jerusalem who led a coalition of five kings against Gibeon and Joshua.
key: Alarmed that Gibeon had made peace with Israel, he called four Amorite kings to attack Gibeon (Joshua 10).
Joshua defeated the coalition, and the LORD threw down great hailstones on the fleeing armies (Joshua 10).
The five kings hid in a cave at Makkedah, and Joshua later put them to death (Joshua 10).

aeneas_106.name: Aeneas
aeneas_106.who: A paralyzed man at Lydda, bedridden for eight years, whom Peter healed in the name of Jesus.
key: Peter found Aeneas at Lydda, paralyzed and bedridden for eight years (Acts 9).
Peter told him Jesus Christ healed him, and Aeneas rose immediately (Acts 9).
All the residents of Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord (Acts 9).

agabus_107.name: Agabus
agabus_107.who: A Christian prophet from Judea who foretold a great famine and Paul's arrest in Jerusalem.
key: Agabus came to Antioch and predicted by the Spirit a great famine over the world (Acts 11).
The famine came under Claudius, and the disciples sent relief to the believers in Judea (Acts 11).
At Caesarea he bound his own hands and feet with Paul's belt, foretelling Paul's arrest (Acts 21).

agur_112.name: Agur
agur_112.who: The son of Jakeh and author of the wise sayings collected in Proverbs 30.
key: The sayings of Agur son of Jakeh open with his confession of limited understanding (Proverbs 30).
He affirms that every word of God proves true and must not be added to (Proverbs 30).
He asks God to give him neither poverty nor riches, only the food he needs (Proverbs 30).
He offers numerical sayings drawn from observing people, animals, and the natural world (Proverbs 30).

ahab_114.name: Ahab
ahab_114.who: A false prophet among the exiles in Babylon, son of Kolaiah, whom Jeremiah condemned for prophesying lies.
key: Jeremiah declared that Ahab and Zedekiah were prophesying lies to the exiles in the LORD's name (Jeremiah 29).
The LORD said Nebuchadnezzar would kill them, and their fate would become a curse among the exiles (Jeremiah 29).
They were condemned for adultery with their neighbors' wives and for speaking words the LORD never gave (Jeremiah 29).

ahasbai_116.name: Ahasbai
ahasbai_116.who: A man of Maacah whose son Eliphelet was one of David's mighty men.
key: Ahasbai is named as the father of Eliphelet in the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
His son Eliphelet belonged to David's elite warriors known as the thirty (2 Samuel 23).

ahaz_119.name: Ahaz
ahaz_119.who: A descendant of King Saul through Jonathan and Mephibosheth, listed in the genealogy of Benjamin.
key: Ahaz was a son of Micah, the son of Merib-baal, Jonathan's son (1 Chronicles 8).
He fathered Jehoaddah, continuing Saul's family line through later generations (1 Chronicles 8).
The genealogy is repeated with his son named Jarah (1 Chronicles 9).

ahijah_136.name: Ahijah
ahijah_136.who: A man of the tribe of Issachar, father of Baasha, who seized the throne of Israel.
key: His son Baasha of Issachar killed King Nadab and struck down Jeroboam's whole house (1 Kings 15).
Baasha son of Ahijah reigned over Israel twenty-four years in Tirzah (1 Kings 15).
Elijah warned that Ahab's house would end like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah (1 Kings 21).
At Jehu's anointing, the prophet declared Ahab's house would become like Baasha's (2 Kings 9).

ahijah_137.name: Ahijah
ahijah_137.who: A son of Jerahmeel in the tribe of Judah, listed in the genealogy of Hezron's descendants.
key: Ahijah is listed among the sons of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2).
Through Hezron and Perez, his family belonged to the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2).

ahiman_146.name: Ahiman
ahiman_146.who: One of the three sons of Anak, the giant Anakim living at Hebron when Israel entered Canaan.
key: Israel's spies found Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, descendants of Anak, living at Hebron (Numbers 13).
Caleb drove out the three sons of Anak from Hebron (Joshua 15).
The men of Judah defeated Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai at Hebron (Judges 1).

ahio_154.name: Ahio
ahio_154.who: A son of Abinadab who helped drive the cart carrying the ark when David first tried to move it.
key: Ahio walked before the ark while he and Uzzah drove the new cart from Abinadab's house (2 Samuel 6).
When the oxen stumbled, Uzzah took hold of the ark, and God struck him down (2 Samuel 6).
Chronicles also records Uzzah and Ahio driving the cart (1 Chronicles 13).

ahisamach_159.name: Ahisamach
ahisamach_159.who: A man of the tribe of Dan, father of the craftsman Oholiab, who helped build the tabernacle.
key: The LORD appointed his son Oholiab of Dan to work with Bezalel on the tabernacle (Exodus 31).
Moses announced that God had given Oholiab son of Ahisamach the ability to teach others (Exodus 35).
His son served as engraver, designer, and embroiderer for the tabernacle (Exodus 38).

akan_179.name: Akan
akan_179.who: A Horite, son of the chief Ezer, among the early inhabitants of Seir.
key: Akan is listed among the sons of Ezer, a descendant of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats his name in the Horite genealogy of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

akkub_182.name: Akkub
akkub_182.who: Ancestor of a family of temple servants whose descendants returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel.
key: The sons of Akkub are listed among the temple servants who returned from exile (Ezra 2).
The temple servants and the sons of Solomon's servants numbered 392 in all (Ezra 2).

alexander_186.name: Alexander
alexander_186.who: A son of Simon of Cyrene, the man compelled to carry Jesus' cross.
key: Mark identifies Simon of Cyrene as the father of Alexander and Rufus (Mark 15).
His father, coming in from the country, was compelled by soldiers to carry Jesus' cross (Mark 15).

alexander_189.name: Alexander
alexander_189.who: A man who rejected faith and a good conscience, whom Paul handed over to Satan.
key: Paul named Hymenaeus and Alexander as men who had made shipwreck of their faith (1 Timothy 1).
Paul handed them over to Satan so they would learn not to blaspheme (1 Timothy 1).
Paul warned Timothy about Alexander the coppersmith, who did him great harm, possibly the same man (2 Timothy 4).

alphaeus_192.name: Alphaeus
alphaeus_192.who: The father of James, one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus.
key: Jesus named James son of Alphaeus among the twelve apostles he sent out (Matthew 10).
Mark's list of the twelve also includes James son of Alphaeus (Mark 3).
Luke names James son of Alphaeus among those Jesus chose as apostles (Luke 6).
After the ascension, James son of Alphaeus prayed with the apostles in Jerusalem (Acts 1).

alvan_195.name: Alvan
alvan_195.who: A Horite, son of Shobal, among the early inhabitants of Seir.
key: Alvan is listed first among the sons of Shobal, son of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats his name in the genealogy of Seir's descendants (1 Chronicles 1).

amariah_198.name: Amariah
amariah_198.who: A priest in Aaron's line, son of Meraioth and grandfather of Zadok, high priest under David.
key: Amariah son of Meraioth is listed in the priestly line from Aaron to the exile (1 Chronicles 6).
His son Ahitub was the father of Zadok, who served as priest under David (1 Chronicles 6).

amariah_199.name: Amariah
amariah_199.who: A priest in Aaron's line, son of Azariah and father of Ahitub, named among Ezra's ancestors.
key: Amariah son of Azariah is listed in the high priestly line descended from Aaron (1 Chronicles 6).
Ezra's genealogy traces his ancestry back to Aaron through Amariah (Ezra 7).

amariah_200.name: Amariah
amariah_200.who: A Levite of Kohath's line, second son of Hebron, listed in David's organization of the Levites.
key: Amariah is named as the second son of Hebron among the Levites David organized (1 Chronicles 23).
He appears again among the Levite family heads who cast lots like the priests (1 Chronicles 24).

amariah_201.name: Amariah
amariah_201.who: The chief priest under King Jehoshaphat, placed over all matters concerning the LORD.
key: Jehoshaphat appointed judges in Jerusalem and charged them to serve in the fear of the LORD (2 Chronicles 19).
He set Amariah the chief priest over every matter of the LORD (2 Chronicles 19).

amasai_210.name: Amasai
amasai_210.who: Chief of the thirty, who pledged loyalty to David when men of Benjamin and Judah joined him.
key: Men of Benjamin and Judah came to David's stronghold, and David questioned their intentions (1 Chronicles 12).
The Spirit clothed Amasai, and he declared loyalty and peace to David and his helpers (1 Chronicles 12).
David received them and made them officers of his troops (1 Chronicles 12).

amaziah_217.name: Amaziah
amaziah_217.who: The priest of Bethel who opposed the prophet Amos during the reign of Jeroboam II.
key: Amaziah reported to Jeroboam that Amos was conspiring against him in Israel (Amos 7).
He told Amos to flee to Judah and stop prophesying at Bethel, the king's sanctuary (Amos 7).
Amos answered that the LORD had called him from tending flocks to prophesy (Amos 7).
Amos then pronounced judgment on Amaziah and his family and foretold Israel's exile (Amos 7).

amittai_219.name: Amittai
amittai_219.who: The father of the prophet Jonah, from Gath-hepher in Israel.
key: His son Jonah of Gath-hepher prophesied that Jeroboam II would restore Israel's borders (2 Kings 14).
The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai to go to Nineveh (Jonah 1).

ammiel_221.name: Ammiel
ammiel_221.who: The father of Machir of Lo-debar, who sheltered Mephibosheth and later supplied David.
key: Mephibosheth was living in the house of Machir son of Ammiel at Lo-debar (2 Samuel 9).
Machir son of Ammiel brought supplies to David at Mahanaim while he fled from Absalom (2 Samuel 17).

anah_247.name: Anah
anah_247.who: The parent of Esau's wife Oholibamah, described as the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite.
key: Esau married Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite (Genesis 36).
Her daughter Oholibamah bore Esau three sons: Jeush, Jalam, and Korah (Genesis 36).

anah_249.name: Anah
anah_249.who: A Horite, son of Zibeon, remembered for finding hot springs in the wilderness.
key: Anah and Aiah are listed as the sons of Zibeon in the line of Seir (Genesis 36).
He found the hot springs in the wilderness while pasturing his father's donkeys (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats his name among the sons of Zibeon (1 Chronicles 1).

ananias_258.name: Ananias
ananias_258.who: A member of the Jerusalem church who died after lying to the Holy Spirit about a gift.
key: With his wife Sapphira's knowledge, Ananias sold property and kept back part of the money (Acts 5).
He brought the rest to the apostles as if it were the full amount (Acts 5).
Peter said he had lied to God, and Ananias fell down and died (Acts 5).
About three hours later Sapphira told the same lie and also died, and great fear came on the church (Acts 5).

anna_268.name: Anna
anna_268.who: An elderly prophetess of the tribe of Asher who recognized the infant Jesus in the temple.
key: Widowed after seven years of marriage, Anna worshiped in the temple with fasting and prayer night and day (Luke 2).
When Jesus was presented at the temple, she came up and gave thanks to God (Luke 2).
She spoke of the child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem (Luke 2).

annas_269.name: Annas
annas_269.who: An influential Jewish high priest, father-in-law of Caiaphas, who questioned Jesus first after his arrest.
key: God's word came to John the Baptist during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas (Luke 3).
After his arrest, Jesus was taken first to Annas, the father-in-law of Caiaphas (John 18).
Annas questioned Jesus about his disciples and teaching, then sent him bound to Caiaphas (John 18).
Annas joined the rulers in questioning Peter and John after a lame man was healed (Acts 4).

arad_281.name: Arad
arad_281.who: A Benjaminite, son of Beriah, listed among the family heads in Benjamin's genealogy.
key: Arad is listed among the sons of Beriah in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8).
His father Beriah was a family head of Aijalon who drove out the inhabitants of Gath (1 Chronicles 8).
He is distinct from the Canaanite king of Arad who attacked Israel in the wilderness (Numbers 21).

aran_288.name: Aran
aran_288.who: A Horite, son of Dishan, among the early inhabitants of Seir.
key: Aran and Uz are listed as the sons of Dishan, a Horite descendant of Seir (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats his name in the genealogy of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

arba_290.name: Arba
arba_290.who: The greatest man among the Anakim and father of Anak, after whom Kiriath-arba (Hebron) was named.
key: Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba, after Arba, the greatest man among the Anakim (Joshua 14).
Caleb received Kiriath-arba as his portion; Arba was the father of Anak (Joshua 15).
Kiriath-arba, that is Hebron, was given to the priests as a city of refuge (Joshua 21).

archelaus_291.name: Archelaus
archelaus_291.who: A son of Herod the Great who ruled Judea after his father's death.
key: After Herod died, Archelaus reigned over Judea in place of his father (Matthew 2).
Joseph was afraid to settle there and, warned in a dream, withdrew to Nazareth in Galilee (Matthew 2).

artaxerxes_313.name: Artaxerxes
artaxerxes_313.who: The Persian king who, after receiving a letter against Jerusalem, ordered the Jews to stop rebuilding the city.
key: Rehum, Shimshai, and their associates wrote to Artaxerxes, accusing Jerusalem of being rebellious (Ezra 4).
Artaxerxes had the records searched and found the city had a history of revolt (Ezra 4).
He ordered the rebuilding stopped, and his officials forced the Jews to cease work (Ezra 4).

artemas_315.name: Artemas
artemas_315.who: A coworker of Paul whom he considered sending to Titus in Crete.
key: Paul planned to send Artemas or Tychicus to Titus (Titus 3).
Once one arrived, Titus was to come quickly to Paul at Nicopolis for the winter (Titus 3).

asaph_329.name: Asaph
asaph_329.who: The father of Joah, the recorder who served King Hezekiah during the Assyrian threat.
key: His son Joah the recorder went with Eliakim and Shebna to meet the Assyrian Rabshakeh (2 Kings 18).
Joah son of Asaph returned with torn clothes and reported the Rabshakeh's words to Hezekiah (2 Kings 18).
Isaiah records the same meeting with Joah son of Asaph (Isaiah 36).

asenath_335.name: Asenath
asenath_335.who: An Egyptian woman, daughter of Potiphera priest of On, who became Joseph's wife.
key: Pharaoh gave Joseph Asenath, daughter of Potiphera priest of On, as his wife (Genesis 41).
Before the famine she bore Joseph two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim (Genesis 41).
Her sons are listed among Jacob's descendants born to Joseph in Egypt (Genesis 46).
